note: The input spells reciprocal then multiply explicitly to retain this regression after division normalization was removed. Six Sinkhorn half-rounds that share one epsilon, in the order row, column, column, row, row, column: no two steps alike, so the recurrence roller leaves them unrolled and fusion keeps one kernel that recomputes each statistic under its reduces. The cut's nested cone passes the epsilon through beside its statistic. Its reader, under a reduce, then takes the epsilon from the workspace while a sibling still binds the same literal in place; both derive the same value, and without the rename that follows a workspace read into what is derived from it they would share one name (nvcc: already declared). Kernel lowering re-spells such a pair positionally, which also moves the piece identities this case pins, so the case fails at `realized` if the cut stops renaming. Found on the DeepSeek V4 post-attention Sinkhorn kernel on a V100, where the prior picked such a row.
